rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands
rows.failure_mode: No movement (window does not move on command)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stays in position. Driver: cannot open or close the window.
rows.cause: H-bridge protection (shoot-through or overcurrent latch) trips falsely on the start inrush and stays latched
rows.rating_reasons: S8: the main function is lost. O4: no field history for this cause, but a new design has an inrush of 14 A at 16 V (DR-1028) and no inrush limit. D6: functional tests would find a lasting latch, but no listed test targets false latching.
rows.recommended_action: Add a spec limit for inrush current (DR-1028). Add a HIL test for repeated start-ups at 16 V and -30 °C that checks the protection does not latch.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands
rows.failure_mode: Degraded: express close stops and reverses with no obstacle in the cold
rows.effect: Vehicle: window reverses part-way up. Driver: cannot close the window on the first try at -20 °C, so the driver is annoyed.
rows.cause: Force estimate and threshold do not allow for the higher friction of cold grease, so normal friction is read as a pinch
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: the main function close is degraded. O8: two open defects at about -20 °C and the ripple filter does not address friction. D6: TP-AP-01 runs at -30 °C but checks stop time and reversal, not false reversal in the cold.
rows.recommended_action: Add a cold false-reversal check (no obstacle, -30 to -10 °C, 9 to 16 V, several closes in a row) to TP-AP-01. Compensate the force offset for temperature and re-check stop time (LL-2021-07).

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands
rows.failure_mode: Intermittent: a short press is read as a held press or the other way round
rows.effect: Vehicle: express runs when manual was meant, or stops after a tap. Driver: window moves further than wanted.
rows.cause: Press-time threshold and debounce of the switch input are mistuned or drift with supply voltage and switch tolerance
rows.rating_reasons: S5: a comfort function is degraded. O4: new design with no history, but a simple function. D6: general tests could find it but none targets the press-time limits across voltage.
rows.recommended_action: Add a HIL test with timed switch presses around the short/held threshold at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, with switch contact bounce.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands
rows.failure_mode: Too late: window reacts late after the switch is pressed
rows.effect: Vehicle: delayed motor start. Driver: the window feels slow, and two drivers complained.
rows.cause: Switch scan and debounce time plus start-up delay are longer than needed and are not specified
rows.rating_reasons: S4: noticed by most customers as feel. O5: two customers reported it, but without measurement. D7: no listed test measures press-to-motor latency.
rows.recommended_action: Measure press-to-motor-start latency on the bench. Add a latency requirement and a HIL test.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands
rows.failure_mode: Too late: motor stays on after switch release
rows.effect: Vehicle: window keeps moving 180 ms after release at 16 V (limit 100 ms). Driver: window overshoots the intended position.
rows.cause: Motor off command is delayed at high supply voltage, for example by a slow driver turn-off or a coast-down or filter delay that depends on voltage
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S5: a comfort function is degraded (overshoot). O9: the defect is open, so the cause has occurred. D4: it was found by a test that covers 16 V, but only some conditions.
rows.recommended_action: Analyse why the release delay is 3 times longer at 16 V than at 13.5 V and fix it in the design. Re-run the release timing test at 9, 13.5 and 16 V.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands
rows.failure_mode: Unintended: express close is available while the window is not normalized
rows.effect: Vehicle: window closes fully with an unreliable position, so the pinch zone and anti-pinch limits are wrong. Driver or passenger: fingers could be pinched where protection is not active, and a legal requirement is broken.
rows.cause: Normalization state defaults to 'normalized' (or is restored from memory) after the battery is disconnected
rows.rating_reasons: S9: the pinch protection may be wrong with a legal requirement broken. O9: the defect is open. D4: a test found it on a battery disconnect, but no listed control targets the normalization state at all power-up cases.
rows.recommended_action: Clear normalization on any power loss or reset and block express close until normalized. Add a HIL test for battery disconnect, brownout and reset, each followed by a short press.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands
rows.failure_mode: Unintended: window moves with no driver command
rows.effect: Vehicle: window closes or opens by itself. Passenger: a hand or child could be trapped, only the anti-pinch protects them.
rows.cause: Switch input read as pressed because of a short to ground or EMI on the switch line with no plausibility check (for example both up and down active)
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury with anti-pinch as the only warning-free protection and a legal requirement. O3: no history, a simple input. D7: tests could find it but none injects switch faults or EMI.
rows.recommended_action: Add a plausibility check for the switch input (up and down together, stuck-on timeout). Add a HIL test with switch line faults and EMI injection.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: Window does not stop at the end stop (end-stop not detected)
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor pushes on the seal until the thermal protection or release. Driver: noise and wear, possibly a stalled motor.
rows.cause: End-stop current threshold is too high for cold or low supply voltage, where the stall current is lower
rows.rating_reasons: S7: the main function is degraded and the motor is stressed. O4: a threshold depends on voltage and temperature but there is no history. D6: end-stop tests are not in the listed controls.
rows.recommended_action: Add end-stop detection tests at 9 V and 16 V and -30 °C and 85 °C. Use a speed-based stop criterion as well as current.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: Degraded: window hits the end position hard (loud knock)
rows.effect: Vehicle: loud impact at the top seal. Driver: noise heard by clinic drivers.
rows.cause: No speed reduction near the end position, and end-stop detection reacts only after contact
rows.rating_reasons: S4: noise noticed by most customers. O8: observed by clinic drivers and no prevention exists. D6: found by a subjective drive but no objective test targets it.
rows.recommended_action: Reduce the speed near the top seal using the position counter. Add an objective impact test (current or sound) at the top.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: Early stop: window stops before it is fully closed
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stays open a few mm or more. Driver: the window does not seal, there may be wind noise or water leaks.
rows.cause: Start current or load peak in the cold crosses the end-stop current threshold and is read as an end stop
rows.rating_reasons: S8: the window cannot close fully. O5: cold stalls were seen on the express close (DR-1004) and are not explained. D6: no listed test targets blanking of the end-stop check.
rows.recommended_action: Define a blanking time and a position window for end-stop detection. Test closes from every position at -30 °C.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Late stop after a pinch at low temperature and low supply voltage
rows.effect: Vehicle: pinch force stays above the 10 ms limit (13 to 14 ms measured). Passenger: a finger or hand could be injured with no warning.
rows.cause: Slow speed sampling and debounce at low motor speed (cold grease and 9 V) delay pinch confirmation, and the fix from LL-2022-02 is not effective in WLC-200
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S10: possible injury with no warning. O9: two open defects and the same cause as LL-2022-02. D3: TP-AP-01 covers the -30 °C and 9 V corner and found it.
rows.recommended_action: Check that the 2 ms sampling below 0 °C and the debounce start (LL-2021-07, LL-2022-02) are present in WLC-200. Shorten the confirmation time at low speed and re-run TP-AP-01 at -30 °C and 9 V on every release.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Reversal distance too short after a pinch at high temperature
rows.effect: Vehicle: window reverses 146 mm at 85 °C (limit 150 mm). Passenger: a trapped hand may not be released enough, a legal requirement is broken.
rows.cause: Reversal distance is set in pulses with no compensation for the higher regulator or motor speed at 85 °C, so the margin is too small
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S9: a legal requirement is broken with a possible injury. O9: the defect is open. D3: TP-AP-01 covers 85 °C and found it.
rows.recommended_action: Raise the reversal distance with a margin over all temperatures and voltages (23 °C gives 162 mm, 85 °C gives 146 mm), and re-run the reversal distance at all TP-AP-01 corners.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Pinch not detected (no stop)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window closes with full force. Passenger: serious injury with no warning.
rows.cause: Force threshold calibration does not cover part-to-part spread of the regulator stiffness, seal aging and the motor constant
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S10: possible injury with no warning. O4: the same algorithm as WLC-100, but unit spread and aging are open questions. D5: TP-AP-01 covers the corners but with one nominal regulator and no aged parts.
rows.recommended_action: Add pinch tests with soft and stiff regulators, aged seals and the tolerance extremes of motor constant. Check the 100 N limit with margin.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Stop time exceeds the limit after a change of threshold, debounce or motor
rows.effect: Vehicle: stop comes later than 10 ms. Passenger: possible injury with no warning.
rows.cause: Debounce margin is lost when the force threshold, debounce or motor is changed and the change is not re-checked
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S10: possible injury with no warning. O5: LL-2021-07 warns of this and the cold defects show the margin is thin. D4: TP-AP-01 would catch it only if it is re-run after each change.
rows.recommended_action: Make a re-run of TP-AP-01 plus the rough-road check a gate for any change of threshold, debounce or motor constants.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: No reversal after a pinch is detected
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor stops but does not reverse and the force stays. Passenger: a hand stays trapped.
rows.cause: Overcurrent protection of the H-bridge shuts the motor off during the direction change, because the pinch current peak is still high
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S10: possible injury with no warning. O3: reversal works in the tests, and no history. D5: TP-AP-01 checks reversal but not at the highest pinch current and a hard-stiffness regulator.
rows.recommended_action: Test reversal at the highest pinch current (16 V, 85 °C, stiff regulator) and check that the current limit allows reversal.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: False reversal on rough roads
rows.effect: Vehicle: window reverses by itself when closing on cobblestones. Driver: cannot close the window on rough roads.
rows.cause: Vibration-induced speed ripple passes the 30 ms debounce, or the filter is not tuned for the WLC-200 motor
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Rough-road vibration HIL profile
rows.rating_reasons: S7: the main function close is degraded. O8: two open defects (2 in 10 tries) and 37 claims in WLC-100 with the same cause. D4: the rough-road profile exists but did not find it before vehicle tests.
rows.recommended_action: Run RR-04 on the HIL with the WLC-200 motor and the current threshold and debounce. Tune the ripple filter and repeat the stop-time check (LL-2021-07).

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Intermittent: controller resets during the reversal
rows.effect: Vehicle: reversal is interrupted by a reset. Passenger: trapped hand not released.
rows.cause: A supply dip while the motor reverses (high current) drops the supply below the reset threshold
rows.rating_reasons: S10: possible injury with no warning. O4: no history, but the reversal draws a high current. D7: no listed test combines a supply dip with a pinch reversal.
rows.recommended_action: Add a HIL test with supply dips during a pinch reversal. Check the reset threshold and supply hold-up in the design.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Position drifts (3.5 mm error at the top seal after 200 cycles)
rows.effect: Vehicle: pinch zone boundary and end positions shift. Driver or passenger: a wrong zone could reduce pinch protection.
rows.cause: Hall pulses are lost or counted twice at direction changes and during coasting after the motor is switched off
prevention: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S7: a main function is degraded because the position is wrong. O9: the defect is open. D4: the endurance run found it but there is no listed test targeting drift.
rows.recommended_action: Count the pulses during coast-down and at reversal. Re-normalize at every end stop. Add a drift check over 1000 cycles.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Hall signal loss not detected in time (motor keeps running)
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor runs 1.2 s until the end stop instead of 200 ms. Passenger: anti-pinch is blind while the window closes, injury is possible with no warning.
rows.cause: The 200 ms plausibility timer restarts on noise pulses at 9 V, where the real pulses are slow, so the loss is hidden
prevention: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
detection: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S10: closing without position or pinch protection can injure with no warning. O9: the defect is open and LL-2023-05 warned of this at 9 V. D3: the Hall removal test at 9 V found it.
rows.recommended_action: Restart the timeout only on plausible pulses (valid period range). Keep the Hall removal test at 9 V and 13.5 V as a gate for each release. Make the connector sealed (LL-2023-05).

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: No DTC stored when the Hall signal is lost
rows.effect: Vehicle: the fault is not in memory and the window keeps pushing on the seal. Driver: no warning, the service has no lead for the fault.
rows.cause: The path from Hall timeout to DTC B1A01 storage is missing or blocked in the WLC-200 software
detection: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S8: window drives on and the fault is hidden, so the thermal protection stops it at last. O9: two open defects. D3: the Hall removal tests found it.
rows.recommended_action: Fix the DTC path for B1A01 and add a check that the DTC is stored and the motor stopped within 200 ms in the Hall removal test.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Intermittent: wrong pulse count from noise or a degraded connector
rows.effect: Vehicle: position jumps or is wrong. Driver: window stops at the wrong place, and the pinch zone may be wrong.
rows.cause: The Hall input has no filtering against noise or contact resistance from a corroded connector, so spurious or missing edges are counted
prevention: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S7: a main function is degraded. O6: connector corrosion happened in WLC-100 (LL-2023-05). D7: tests remove the signal but do not inject noise or edge errors.
rows.recommended_action: Add a HIL test with noise and dropped pulses on the Hall input. Add a pulse period plausibility check and a hardware filter.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Position lost or stale after a reset during movement
rows.effect: Vehicle: position is not the real one after wake-up. Driver: express and pinch zone use a wrong position.
rows.cause: Position is stored in memory only at the end of a movement, so a reset or brownout during motion leaves an old value that is still marked valid
rows.rating_reasons: S8: wrong position can leave the pinch zone wrong. O4: no history. D7: no test resets the controller during a movement.
rows.recommended_action: Mark position invalid when a movement starts and valid when it ends. Add a HIL test with resets at random times during movement.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Opening is allowed once above the 140 °C block limit
rows.effect: Vehicle: one extra opening at 143 °C. Driver: motor is stressed, a shorter life.
rows.cause: The block decision reads a stale estimate before the thermal task has run (the same cause as LL-2024-01 in the shared platform module)
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: motor protection is degraded and it could lose the main function. O9: two open defects and the platform fix from LL-2024-01 seems missing. D3: TC-TH-03 found it.
rows.recommended_action: Check the LL-2024-01 fix (the block decision reads the estimate after the thermal task) in WLC-200 and keep the 'request right after the limit' test.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Estimated temperature lower than the real motor temperature
rows.effect: Vehicle: current is not limited and the motor overheats. Driver: motor damage and a lost window function.
rows.cause: Thermal model parameters (thermal mass, cooling) are not valid for high ambient temperature or for unit spread
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S8: motor damage means the main function is lost. O4: the model is new for WLC-200 and the platform has an old fix. D4: TP-TH-01 targets it but at some conditions only.
rows.recommended_action: Extend TP-TH-01 to 85 °C ambient, repeated movements and a high-friction regulator.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Estimated temperature higher than real: current limited or opening blocked without need
rows.effect: Vehicle: window slow or opening refused. Driver: loses the window function while the motor is cool.
rows.cause: Thermal model is too conservative at high ambient temperature, or the estimate has an offset that grows over cycles
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded. O4: no history. D5: TP-TH-01 compares to thermocouples but does not target the long-run drift.
rows.recommended_action: Add a long-run comparison to thermocouple data in TP-TH-01 and check the estimate for drift.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Estimate lost at reset or power cycle
rows.effect: Vehicle: after wake-up the model assumes a cool motor, so a hot motor is moved. Driver: motor overheats.
rows.cause: The temperature estimate is held in RAM and initialised to ambient at every start
rows.rating_reasons: S7: motor protection is degraded. O5: a plausible design weakness, no history. D8: no test resets the controller while the model is hot.
rows.recommended_action: Keep the estimate through short power losses or use a conservative start value after a reset, and add a HIL test that resets at a hot model.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: WLC_Status frame missing during diagnostic requests
rows.effect: Vehicle: a 200 ms gap in WLC_Status. Driver: the body controller may show a wrong window state, mainly in the workshop.
rows.cause: The CAN transmit queue is filled by diagnostic responses and a status frame is dropped, so the LL-2024-09 fix is not complete in WLC-200
prevention: CAN transmit queue sized for the worst-case bus load (from LL-2024-09)
rows.rating_reasons: S5: a comfort-level reporting function is degraded. O8: open defect in spite of the prevention. D3: TC-DG-03 found it, with diagnostic load.
rows.recommended_action: Check the queue calculation and the own transmit buffer for status frames, as LL-2024-09 requires. Repeat TC-DG-03 with a longer run and worst-case bus load.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: No fault reported or stored on overcurrent (DTC B1A02 and fault state missing)
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor stops but fault state remains 0. Driver: no warning, and the service cannot find the fault.
rows.cause: The overcurrent detection stops the motor but does not call the DTC storage or set the status fault state
rows.rating_reasons: S5: reporting is lost but the motor stops safely. O9: two open defects. D3: TC-DG-02 and the injection test found it.
rows.recommended_action: Connect the overcurrent detection to DTC B1A02 and the WLC_Status fault bit. Extend TC-DG-02 to check both.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: Unintended: WLC_CloseAll executed from a corrupted or false frame
rows.effect: Vehicle: window closes with no driver request. Passenger: possible pinch, only the anti-pinch protects.
rows.cause: WLC_CloseAll is accepted with no alive counter or CRC check and without a plausibility check of the vehicle state
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury and a legal requirement for unrequested closing. O3: no history and a CAN frame is protected by CRC at the bus level. D7: no test injects false CloseAll frames.
rows.recommended_action: Add an alive counter and CRC check for WLC_CloseAll, and a HIL test that sends corrupted, repeated and out-of-state frames.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: WLC_CloseAll received but ignored
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stays open when the vehicle is locked. Driver: window stays open and comfort closing is lost.
rows.cause: CloseAll is rejected in a state check (for example not normalized or manual-only mode) with no feedback in the status
rows.rating_reasons: S6: a comfort function is lost. O4: no history. D6: tests could find it but none targets the rejection cases.
rows.recommended_action: Test CloseAll in all states (not normalized, low voltage, thermal limit) and report a rejection in WLC_Status.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: Diagnostic response too late (55 to 62 ms, limit 50 ms)
rows.effect: Vehicle: some diagnostic answers come late. Driver: not noticed, a service tool may time out.
rows.cause: The diagnostic task is delayed by the motor start-up load (interrupts and the current measurement)
rows.rating_reasons: S3: only a service user may notice. O8: the defect is open (3 in 100). D3: the diagnostic request test found it.
rows.recommended_action: Review the task priorities and interrupt load during motor start. Repeat the 100-request test during start-ups.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: WLC_Status shows stale or wrong content (position, state) after a reset or in a fault
rows.effect: Vehicle: the body controller sees a wrong window state. Driver: wrong displays or wrong comfort functions.
rows.cause: The status signals are filled before the first valid calculation after wake-up and are not marked invalid
rows.rating_reasons: S5: a comfort function is degraded. O4: no history. D7: tests check the cycle time but not content after a reset.
rows.recommended_action: Send an 'invalid' value until the first valid calculation and test the content after a reset and a brownout.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Motor not stopped in time at undervoltage
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor continues with a supply too low for reliable anti-pinch. Passenger: possible injury.
rows.cause: Undervoltage threshold or the filter on the supply measurement is too slow, so the motor stop takes longer than 50 ms
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury with a legal requirement. O3: the stop was 21 ms against the 50 ms limit (DR-1025), a good margin. D4: a test targets it, but only at one drop to 5.5 V.
rows.recommended_action: Extend the undervoltage test to different drop rates, start levels and temperatures.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Intermittent: mode switches between full and manual-only near the threshold
rows.effect: Vehicle: express and anti-pinch switch on and off during a movement. Driver: window stops or runs unexpectedly.
rows.cause: The supply monitor has no hysteresis or hold time at the thresholds of WLC-001 to WLC-003, and the motor load causes the voltage to dip
rows.rating_reasons: S7: a main function is degraded. O5: no history but a motor start dips the supply. D7: no listed test ramps the voltage slowly through the thresholds under load.
rows.recommended_action: Add hysteresis and a hold time. Add a HIL test with slow voltage ramps and noise through each threshold during a movement.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Overvoltage or load dump not handled
rows.effect: Vehicle: controller damage or a wrong motor action. Driver: window lost, possibly stuck.
rows.cause: Overvoltage protection and the high-voltage threshold are not specified or tested above 16 V
rows.rating_reasons: S8: window lost. O4: new design with standard protection parts. D8: the HIL tests stop at 16 V and no load dump test is listed.
rows.recommended_action: Add a load dump and jump-start test (above 16 V) and a requirement for the behaviour at high voltage.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Controller dead after reverse polarity
rows.effect: Vehicle: controller does not wake up after -14 V for 60 s. Driver: window cannot be moved at all.
rows.cause: Reverse polarity protection diode D3 is too small for the energy of -14 V for 60 s and fails open
rows.rating_reasons: S8: the main function is lost. O9: the defect is open on the diode. D3: the reverse polarity test found it.
rows.recommended_action: Re-dimension D3 (or add a series protection) for -14 V for 60 s, and repeat the reverse polarity test on a number of samples.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Intermittent: controller resets during the reversal
rows.effect: Vehicle: reversal is interrupted by a reset. Passenger: trapped hand not released.
rows.cause: A supply dip while the motor reverses (high current) drops the supply below the reset threshold
rows.rating_reasons: S10: possible injury with no warning. O4: no history, but the reversal draws a high current. D7: no listed test combines a supply dip with a pinch reversal.
rows.recommended_action: Add a HIL test with supply dips during a pinch reversal. Check the reset threshold and supply hold-up in the design.

prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S10: possible injury with no warning. O9: two open defects and the same cause as LL-2022-02. D3: TP-AP-01 covers the -30 °C and 9 V corner and found it.
rows.recommended_action: Check that the 2 ms sampling below 0 °C and the debounce start (LL-2021-07, LL-2022-02) are present in WLC-200. Shorten the confirmation time at low speed and re-run TP-AP-01 at -30 °C and 9 V on every release.

rows.effect: Vehicle: motor runs 1.2 s until the end stop instead of 200 ms. Passenger: anti-pinch is blind while the window closes, injury is possible with no warning.
rows.cause: The 200 ms plausibility timer restarts on noise pulses at 9 V, where the real pulses are slow, so the loss is hidden
prevention: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
detection: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S10: closing without position or pinch protection can injure with no warning. O9: the defect is open and LL-2023-05 warned of this at 9 V. D3: the Hall removal test at 9 V found it.

rows.failure_mode: Pinch not detected (no stop)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window closes with full force. Passenger: serious injury with no warning.
rows.cause: Force threshold calibration does not cover part-to-part spread of the regulator stiffness, seal aging and the motor constant
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S10: possible injury with no warning. O4: the same algorithm as WLC-100, but unit spread and aging are open questions. D5: TP-AP-01 covers the corners but with one nominal regulator and no aged parts.
rows.recommended_action: Add pinch tests with soft and stiff regulators, aged seals and the tolerance extremes of motor constant. Check the 100 N limit with margin.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Stop time exceeds the limit after a change of threshold, debounce or motor
rows.effect: Vehicle: stop comes later than 10 ms. Passenger: possible injury with no warning.
rows.cause: Debounce margin is lost when the force threshold, debounce or motor is changed and the change is not re-checked
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S10: possible injury with no warning. O5: LL-2021-07 warns of this and the cold defects show the margin is thin. D4: TP-AP-01 would catch it only if it is re-run after each change.
rows.recommended_action: Make a re-run of TP-AP-01 plus the rough-road check a gate for any change of threshold, debounce or motor constants.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: No reversal after a pinch is detected
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor stops but does not reverse and the force stays. Passenger: a hand stays trapped.
rows.cause: Overcurrent protection of the H-bridge shuts the motor off during the direction change, because the pinch current peak is still high
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S10: possible injury with no warning. O3: reversal works in the tests, and no history. D5: TP-AP-01 checks reversal but not at the highest pinch current and a hard-stiffness regulator.
rows.recommended_action: Test reversal at the highest pinch current (16 V, 85 °C, stiff regulator) and check that the current limit allows reversal.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands
rows.failure_mode: Unintended: express close is available while the window is not normalized
rows.effect: Vehicle: window closes fully with an unreliable position, so the pinch zone and anti-pinch limits are wrong. Driver or passenger: fingers could be pinched where protection is not active, and a legal requirement is broken.
rows.cause: Normalization state defaults to 'normalized' (or is restored from memory) after the battery is disconnected
rows.rating_reasons: S9: the pinch protection may be wrong with a legal requirement broken. O9: the defect is open. D4: a test found it on a battery disconnect, but no listed control targets the normalization state at all power-up cases.
rows.recommended_action: Clear normalization on any power loss or reset and block express close until normalized. Add a HIL test for battery disconnect, brownout and reset, each followed by a short press.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: Reversal distance too short after a pinch at high temperature
rows.effect: Vehicle: window reverses 146 mm at 85 °C (limit 150 mm). Passenger: a trapped hand may not be released enough, a legal requirement is broken.
rows.cause: Reversal distance is set in pulses with no compensation for the higher regulator or motor speed at 85 °C, so the margin is too small
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S9: a legal requirement is broken with a possible injury. O9: the defect is open. D3: TP-AP-01 covers 85 °C and found it.
rows.recommended_action: Raise the reversal distance with a margin over all temperatures and voltages (23 °C gives 162 mm, 85 °C gives 146 mm), and re-run the reversal distance at all TP-AP-01 corners.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands
rows.failure_mode: Unintended: window moves with no driver command
rows.effect: Vehicle: window closes or opens by itself. Passenger: a hand or child could be trapped, only the anti-pinch protects them.
rows.cause: Switch input read as pressed because of a short to ground or EMI on the switch line with no plausibility check (for example both up and down active)
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury with anti-pinch as the only warning-free protection and a legal requirement. O3: no history, a simple input. D7: tests could find it but none injects switch faults or EMI.
rows.recommended_action: Add a plausibility check for the switch input (up and down together, stuck-on timeout). Add a HIL test with switch line faults and EMI injection.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: Unintended: WLC_CloseAll executed from a corrupted or false frame
rows.effect: Vehicle: window closes with no driver request. Passenger: possible pinch, only the anti-pinch protects.
rows.cause: WLC_CloseAll is accepted with no alive counter or CRC check and without a plausibility check of the vehicle state
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury and a legal requirement for unrequested closing. O3: no history and a CAN frame is protected by CRC at the bus level. D7: no test injects false CloseAll frames.
rows.recommended_action: Add an alive counter and CRC check for WLC_CloseAll, and a HIL test that sends corrupted, repeated and out-of-state frames.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Motor not stopped in time at undervoltage
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor continues with a supply too low for reliable anti-pinch. Passenger: possible injury.
rows.cause: Undervoltage threshold or the filter on the supply measurement is too slow, so the motor stop takes longer than 50 ms
rows.rating_reasons: S9: possible injury with a legal requirement. O3: the stop was 21 ms against the 50 ms limit (DR-1025), a good margin. D4: a test targets it, but only at one drop to 5.5 V.
rows.recommended_action: Extend the undervoltage test to different drop rates, start levels and temperatures.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Overvoltage or load dump not handled
rows.effect: Vehicle: controller damage or a wrong motor action. Driver: window lost, possibly stuck.
rows.cause: Overvoltage protection and the high-voltage threshold are not specified or tested above 16 V
rows.rating_reasons: S8: window lost. O4: new design with standard protection parts. D8: the HIL tests stop at 16 V and no load dump test is listed.
rows.recommended_action: Add a load dump and jump-start test (above 16 V) and a requirement for the behaviour at high voltage.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: Early stop: window stops before it is fully closed
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stays open a few mm or more. Driver: the window does not seal, there may be wind noise or water leaks.
rows.cause: Start current or load peak in the cold crosses the end-stop current threshold and is read as an end stop
rows.rating_reasons: S8: the window cannot close fully. O5: cold stalls were seen on the express close (DR-1004) and are not explained. D6: no listed test targets blanking of the end-stop check.
rows.recommended_action: Define a blanking time and a position window for end-stop detection. Test closes from every position at -30 °C.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Position lost or stale after a reset during movement
rows.effect: Vehicle: position is not the real one after wake-up. Driver: express and pinch zone use a wrong position.
rows.cause: Position is stored in memory only at the end of a movement, so a reset or brownout during motion leaves an old value that is still marked valid
rows.rating_reasons: S8: wrong position can leave the pinch zone wrong. O4: no history. D7: no test resets the controller during a movement.
rows.recommended_action: Mark position invalid when a movement starts and valid when it ends. Add a HIL test with resets at random times during movement.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: No DTC stored when the Hall signal is lost
rows.effect: Vehicle: the fault is not in memory and the window keeps pushing on the seal. Driver: no warning, the service has no lead for the fault.
rows.cause: The path from Hall timeout to DTC B1A01 storage is missing or blocked in the WLC-200 software
detection: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S8: window drives on and the fault is hidden, so the thermal protection stops it at last. O9: two open defects. D3: the Hall removal tests found it.
rows.recommended_action: Fix the DTC path for B1A01 and add a check that the DTC is stored and the motor stopped within 200 ms in the Hall removal test.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Controller dead after reverse polarity
rows.effect: Vehicle: controller does not wake up after -14 V for 60 s. Driver: window cannot be moved at all.
rows.cause: Reverse polarity protection diode D3 is too small for the energy of -14 V for 60 s and fails open
rows.rating_reasons: S8: the main function is lost. O9: the defect is open on the diode. D3: the reverse polarity test found it.
rows.recommended_action: Re-dimension D3 (or add a series protection) for -14 V for 60 s, and repeat the reverse polarity test on a number of samples.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands
rows.failure_mode: No movement (window does not move on command)
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stays in position. Driver: cannot open or close the window.
rows.cause: H-bridge protection (shoot-through or overcurrent latch) trips falsely on the start inrush and stays latched
rows.rating_reasons: S8: the main function is lost. O4: no field history for this cause, but a new design has an inrush of 14 A at 16 V (DR-1028) and no inrush limit. D6: functional tests would find a lasting latch, but no listed test targets false latching.
rows.recommended_action: Add a spec limit for inrush current (DR-1028). Add a HIL test for repeated start-ups at 16 V and -30 °C that checks the protection does not latch.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Estimated temperature lower than the real motor temperature
rows.effect: Vehicle: current is not limited and the motor overheats. Driver: motor damage and a lost window function.
rows.cause: Thermal model parameters (thermal mass, cooling) are not valid for high ambient temperature or for unit spread
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S8: motor damage means the main function is lost. O4: the model is new for WLC-200 and the platform has an old fix. D4: TP-TH-01 targets it but at some conditions only.
rows.recommended_action: Extend TP-TH-01 to 85 °C ambient, repeated movements and a high-friction regulator.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands
rows.failure_mode: Degraded: express close stops and reverses with no obstacle in the cold
rows.effect: Vehicle: window reverses part-way up. Driver: cannot close the window on the first try at -20 °C, so the driver is annoyed.
rows.cause: Force estimate and threshold do not allow for the higher friction of cold grease, so normal friction is read as a pinch
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: the main function close is degraded. O8: two open defects at about -20 °C and the ripple filter does not address friction. D6: TP-AP-01 runs at -30 °C but checks stop time and reversal, not false reversal in the cold.
rows.recommended_action: Add a cold false-reversal check (no obstacle, -30 to -10 °C, 9 to 16 V, several closes in a row) to TP-AP-01. Compensate the force offset for temperature and re-check stop time (LL-2021-07).

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Intermittent: wrong pulse count from noise or a degraded connector
rows.effect: Vehicle: position jumps or is wrong. Driver: window stops at the wrong place, and the pinch zone may be wrong.
rows.cause: The Hall input has no filtering against noise or contact resistance from a corroded connector, so spurious or missing edges are counted
prevention: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S7: a main function is degraded. O6: connector corrosion happened in WLC-100 (LL-2023-05). D7: tests remove the signal but do not inject noise or edge errors.
rows.recommended_action: Add a HIL test with noise and dropped pulses on the Hall input. Add a pulse period plausibility check and a hardware filter.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Estimate lost at reset or power cycle
rows.effect: Vehicle: after wake-up the model assumes a cool motor, so a hot motor is moved. Driver: motor overheats.
rows.cause: The temperature estimate is held in RAM and initialised to ambient at every start
rows.rating_reasons: S7: motor protection is degraded. O5: a plausible design weakness, no history. D8: no test resets the controller while the model is hot.
rows.recommended_action: Keep the estimate through short power losses or use a conservative start value after a reset, and add a HIL test that resets at a hot model.

rows.function: 4. Keep track of window position
rows.failure_mode: Position drifts (3.5 mm error at the top seal after 200 cycles)
rows.effect: Vehicle: pinch zone boundary and end positions shift. Driver or passenger: a wrong zone could reduce pinch protection.
rows.cause: Hall pulses are lost or counted twice at direction changes and during coasting after the motor is switched off
prevention: Hall signal plausibility check, 200 ms timeout
rows.rating_reasons: S7: a main function is degraded because the position is wrong. O9: the defect is open. D4: the endurance run found it but there is no listed test targeting drift.
rows.recommended_action: Count the pulses during coast-down and at reversal. Re-normalize at every end stop. Add a drift check over 1000 cycles.

rows.function: 7. Behave safely at low and high supply voltage
rows.failure_mode: Intermittent: mode switches between full and manual-only near the threshold
rows.effect: Vehicle: express and anti-pinch switch on and off during a movement. Driver: window stops or runs unexpectedly.
rows.cause: The supply monitor has no hysteresis or hold time at the thresholds of WLC-001 to WLC-003, and the motor load causes the voltage to dip
rows.rating_reasons: S7: a main function is degraded. O5: no history but a motor start dips the supply. D7: no listed test ramps the voltage slowly through the thresholds under load.
rows.recommended_action: Add hysteresis and a hold time. Add a HIL test with slow voltage ramps and noise through each threshold during a movement.

rows.function: 3. Detect a pinch and reverse the window
rows.failure_mode: False reversal on rough roads
rows.effect: Vehicle: window reverses by itself when closing on cobblestones. Driver: cannot close the window on rough roads.
rows.cause: Vibration-induced speed ripple passes the 30 ms debounce, or the filter is not tuned for the WLC-200 motor
prevention: Speed-ripple filter with 30 ms debounce (from LL-2021-07)
detection: Rough-road vibration HIL profile
rows.rating_reasons: S7: the main function close is degraded. O8: two open defects (2 in 10 tries) and 37 claims in WLC-100 with the same cause. D4: the rough-road profile exists but did not find it before vehicle tests.
rows.recommended_action: Run RR-04 on the HIL with the WLC-200 motor and the current threshold and debounce. Tune the ripple filter and repeat the stop-time check (LL-2021-07).

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Opening is allowed once above the 140 °C block limit
rows.effect: Vehicle: one extra opening at 143 °C. Driver: motor is stressed, a shorter life.
rows.cause: The block decision reads a stale estimate before the thermal task has run (the same cause as LL-2024-01 in the shared platform module)
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: motor protection is degraded and it could lose the main function. O9: two open defects and the platform fix from LL-2024-01 seems missing. D3: TC-TH-03 found it.
rows.recommended_action: Check the LL-2024-01 fix (the block decision reads the estimate after the thermal task) in WLC-200 and keep the 'request right after the limit' test.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: Window does not stop at the end stop (end-stop not detected)
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor pushes on the seal until the thermal protection or release. Driver: noise and wear, possibly a stalled motor.
rows.cause: End-stop current threshold is too high for cold or low supply voltage, where the stall current is lower
rows.rating_reasons: S7: the main function is degraded and the motor is stressed. O4: a threshold depends on voltage and temperature but there is no history. D6: end-stop tests are not in the listed controls.
rows.recommended_action: Add end-stop detection tests at 9 V and 16 V and -30 °C and 85 °C. Use a speed-based stop criterion as well as current.

rows.function: 5. Protect the motor from overheating
rows.failure_mode: Estimated temperature higher than real: current limited or opening blocked without need
rows.effect: Vehicle: window slow or opening refused. Driver: loses the window function while the motor is cool.
rows.cause: Thermal model is too conservative at high ambient temperature, or the estimate has an offset that grows over cycles
detection: Thermal model reviewed against thermocouple data (TP-TH-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S7: main function degraded. O4: no history. D5: TP-TH-01 compares to thermocouples but does not target the long-run drift.
rows.recommended_action: Add a long-run comparison to thermocouple data in TP-TH-01 and check the estimate for drift.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: WLC_CloseAll received but ignored
rows.effect: Vehicle: window stays open when the vehicle is locked. Driver: window stays open and comfort closing is lost.
rows.cause: CloseAll is rejected in a state check (for example not normalized or manual-only mode) with no feedback in the status
rows.rating_reasons: S6: a comfort function is lost. O4: no history. D6: tests could find it but none targets the rejection cases.
rows.recommended_action: Test CloseAll in all states (not normalized, low voltage, thermal limit) and report a rejection in WLC_Status.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands
rows.failure_mode: Too late: motor stays on after switch release
rows.effect: Vehicle: window keeps moving 180 ms after release at 16 V (limit 100 ms). Driver: window overshoots the intended position.
rows.cause: Motor off command is delayed at high supply voltage, for example by a slow driver turn-off or a coast-down or filter delay that depends on voltage
detection: Anti-pinch HIL tests at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, -30, 23 and 85 °C (TP-AP-01)
rows.rating_reasons: S5: a comfort function is degraded (overshoot). O9: the defect is open, so the cause has occurred. D4: it was found by a test that covers 16 V, but only some conditions.
rows.recommended_action: Analyse why the release delay is 3 times longer at 16 V than at 13.5 V and fix it in the design. Re-run the release timing test at 9, 13.5 and 16 V.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: WLC_Status shows stale or wrong content (position, state) after a reset or in a fault
rows.effect: Vehicle: the body controller sees a wrong window state. Driver: wrong displays or wrong comfort functions.
rows.cause: The status signals are filled before the first valid calculation after wake-up and are not marked invalid
rows.rating_reasons: S5: a comfort function is degraded. O4: no history. D7: tests check the cycle time but not content after a reset.
rows.recommended_action: Send an 'invalid' value until the first valid calculation and test the content after a reset and a brownout.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: No fault reported or stored on overcurrent (DTC B1A02 and fault state missing)
rows.effect: Vehicle: motor stops but fault state remains 0. Driver: no warning, and the service cannot find the fault.
rows.cause: The overcurrent detection stops the motor but does not call the DTC storage or set the status fault state
rows.rating_reasons: S5: reporting is lost but the motor stops safely. O9: two open defects. D3: TC-DG-02 and the injection test found it.
rows.recommended_action: Connect the overcurrent detection to DTC B1A02 and the WLC_Status fault bit. Extend TC-DG-02 to check both.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands
rows.failure_mode: Intermittent: a short press is read as a held press or the other way round
rows.effect: Vehicle: express runs when manual was meant, or stops after a tap. Driver: window moves further than wanted.
rows.cause: Press-time threshold and debounce of the switch input are mistuned or drift with supply voltage and switch tolerance
rows.rating_reasons: S5: a comfort function is degraded. O4: new design with no history, but a simple function. D6: general tests could find it but none targets the press-time limits across voltage.
rows.recommended_action: Add a HIL test with timed switch presses around the short/held threshold at 9, 13.5 and 16 V, with switch contact bounce.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: WLC_Status frame missing during diagnostic requests
rows.effect: Vehicle: a 200 ms gap in WLC_Status. Driver: the body controller may show a wrong window state, mainly in the workshop.
rows.cause: The CAN transmit queue is filled by diagnostic responses and a status frame is dropped, so the LL-2024-09 fix is not complete in WLC-200
prevention: CAN transmit queue sized for the worst-case bus load (from LL-2024-09)
rows.rating_reasons: S5: a comfort-level reporting function is degraded. O8: open defect in spite of the prevention. D3: TC-DG-03 found it, with diagnostic load.
rows.recommended_action: Check the queue calculation and the own transmit buffer for status frames, as LL-2024-09 requires. Repeat TC-DG-03 with a longer run and worst-case bus load.

rows.function: 2. Stop the window at the end positions
rows.failure_mode: Degraded: window hits the end position hard (loud knock)
rows.effect: Vehicle: loud impact at the top seal. Driver: noise heard by clinic drivers.
rows.cause: No speed reduction near the end position, and end-stop detection reacts only after contact
rows.rating_reasons: S4: noise noticed by most customers. O8: observed by clinic drivers and no prevention exists. D6: found by a subjective drive but no objective test targets it.
rows.recommended_action: Reduce the speed near the top seal using the position counter. Add an objective impact test (current or sound) at the top.

rows.function: 1. Move the window as the driver commands
rows.failure_mode: Too late: window reacts late after the switch is pressed
rows.effect: Vehicle: delayed motor start. Driver: the window feels slow, and two drivers complained.
rows.cause: Switch scan and debounce time plus start-up delay are longer than needed and are not specified
rows.rating_reasons: S4: noticed by most customers as feel. O5: two customers reported it, but without measurement. D7: no listed test measures press-to-motor latency.
rows.recommended_action: Measure press-to-motor-start latency on the bench. Add a latency requirement and a HIL test.

rows.function: 6. Report status and faults to the body controller
rows.failure_mode: Diagnostic response too late (55 to 62 ms, limit 50 ms)
rows.effect: Vehicle: some diagnostic answers come late. Driver: not noticed, a service tool may time out.
rows.cause: The diagnostic task is delayed by the motor start-up load (interrupts and the current measurement)
rows.rating_reasons: S3: only a service user may notice. O8: the defect is open (3 in 100). D3: the diagnostic request test found it.
rows.recommended_action: Review the task priorities and interrupt load during motor start. Repeat the 100-request test during start-ups.

problems: function not analysed: Detect a pinch in the pinch zone and reverse the window
